distinct_patches.rule: held-out candidates with the same graded patch (or the same code apart from comments and docstrings, labels/duplicates.json) count once; the representative is the pre-correction state, else the first id

labelers.construction: construction intent for constructed candidates; the observed pre-correction states keep their D19 label (protocol v0.3 policy)
labelers.construction_constructed_only: construction intent; defined for constructed candidates only
labelers.refcheck: reference-check verdict: valid iff every independent reference check passes (regression norm not included)

meta.label_policy: automated pilot: D19 rule proposals and the other recorded labelings; no human labels
meta.protocol: experiments/protocol.md v0.7 §15.1 (re-analyses of pilot-v0.3.3 are post hoc and exploratory) and §15.7 (reporting rules)

natural_negatives.population: observed pre-correction states labeled invalid by D19 (the pilot has no other natural negative)

oracle_gated.explanation: Per-arm gating drops only the cells of an arm that fails its own reference (C1 loses CS-01, C2 loses CS-01), so C1 keeps 5/11 invalid and 0/8 valid candidates. The design audit's figures for C3/C4 are the common-support counts of their comparison with C1, which drops the same families for both arms. Per arm, C3 keeps 0/17 invalid and 0/10 valid; C4 keeps 0/17 invalid and 0/10 valid.
oracle_gated.rule: drop a verifier x task cell when the verifier does not pass the task's reference solution in the run's sanity grading

paired_comparisons.direction: p_greater tests H1: A - B > 0, i.e. the first-named arm of protocol §7 errs more

statistics.family_mean: sum over families of the rate difference A - B (each family weighs the same)
statistics.pooled: sum over families of the count difference A - B (the pooled difference times n)

notes.llm_freeform: B2's checks map to its own requirement list, which has no mapping to the reference contract: not evaluable; only the reference-passing criterion is reported
notes.repo_tests: B1 has no requirement map; this re-analysis maps its checks from the base commit's own tests to the regression norm (REGRESSION) and its agent-added checks to nothing

right_reason.rule: a rejection of an invalid candidate counts only if at least one failing check passes on the task's reference solution and maps, through the verifier's requirement map and the contract mapping (mapper 1; mapper 2 as a sensitivity), to a requirement the candidate violates (its D19 violated list, plus REGRESSION when the regression norm failed); other rejections count as acceptances
